A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sketch-of-Thought work by the same authors. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization and expansion.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy and token-usage experiments across 15 text datasets, three Qwen model sizes, multilingual evaluations, and ScienceQA, including Self-Consistency comparisons.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments across additional model families and comparison methods, plus GQA, extended reasoning pipelines, and router evaluations in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The three paradigms, DistilBERT router, labeling approach, and router training objective remain. v2 adds limited procedural adaptations for Self-Refine and Multi-Agent Debate, including critique, revision, and agent interaction prompts (Appendices B.6 and C). The original paradigm prompts are retained with presentation edits.

E1.justification: v2 adds GQA visual question answering alongside the retained ScienceQA evaluation. The 15 primary text datasets and Korean, Italian, and German evaluations remain. CommonsenseQA's appearance in the expanded dataset-information table is additional documentation; it was already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds directly relevant token-efficient comparators, Chain-of-Draft and CCoT-45, to the main experiments. CCoT was only discussed in v1. It also adds paired CoT/SoT comparisons within Self-Refine and Multi-Agent Debate, substantially expanding comparison beyond v1's CoT and Self-Consistency evaluations.

E3.justification: Primary evaluation expands beyond Qwen to LLaMA, GPT-4o, and Claude. Token counting changes from reasoning-only tokens to all generated tokens, including final answers. Table 5 revises v1's blanket test-split description with validation and held-out training subsets for several datasets. New protocols include router testing and multi-turn refinement/debate. These reported changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 newly evaluates router agreement with GPT-4o labels on 2,250 examples, presenting a confusion matrix and class-specific analysis. Appendix D adds dataset-level paradigm distributions, expected-versus-dominant assignments, and routing examples. Appendix E adds comparative output cases. These substantially expand analysis of the central routing component beyond v1's illustrative examples.

E5.justification: v2 first reports averaging three independent runs per question and discloses random seed 42. v1's three-path specification concerned Self-Consistency rather than general repeated-run reporting. This is additional disclosure, not evidence of increased runs; neither version supplies confidence intervals, significance tests, or dispersion estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive results for new models, baselines, GQA, refinement/debate, router evaluation, and individual datasets. Reported Qwen-32B overall SoT/CoT accuracies change from 80.49/80.95 to 82.30/82.24; ScienceQA values also change. These are revised results under changed reported protocols, not established same-setting gains. Multilingual numerical results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The LLM, prompting, sketched-reasoning, and routing formulations retain their mathematical substance. Revisions clarify notation and exposition; neither version contains substantive theorems or proofs, and v2 adds no new theoretical derivation.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains cognitively structured, adaptively selected prompting that reduces tokens while preserving accuracy. The abstract and introduction update the saving headline from 76% to up to 78%, and the conclusion explicitly emphasizes ensemble compatibility. However, v2's conclusion still reports up to 76%.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of model-family differences, compression baselines, conservative routing, and GQA's visual-grounding difficulties. It removes v1's explicit medical-calibration warning and Qwen-only limitation, while adding concerns about paradigm coverage, interpretability, and GPT-generated labeling biases. The earlier 70–80% inference-cost extrapolation also disappears, substantially revising applicability and limitation discussions.

D1.justification: Expanded appendices disclose dataset subsets and sample counts, checkpoint/API identifiers, GPU/CUDA/precision information, exemplar-selection procedures, and router and extended-strategy prompts. The original paradigm prompts and code-access link are retained. Some detail is lost: v1's explicit three-path Self-Consistency specification is no longer stated.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chain-of-Draft and references supporting the new models, dataset, evaluation, and ensemble experiments, while removing discussions such as LeanContext and automatic prompt optimization. Related work more explicitly contrasts SoT with compression heuristics, but its central positioning as cognitive, task-adaptive output structuring remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, preliminaries, experimental setup, results, and related work are extensively rewritten. Router training moves into the method discussion, experiments are reorganized around baselines and protocol, limitations follow the conclusion, and the appendices are reorganized into setup, prompting, results, routing analysis, and examples.

P2.justification: Figure 1 expands its model display, and Figure 2 is redrawn to compare four prompting workflows. The main table is substantially redesigned, with ensemble results separated. New displays include router confusion and distribution analyses, per-dataset results, and output comparisons. Existing paradigm prompt boxes are reformatted and presented as numbered figures.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important weaknesses in v1: evaluation confined to Qwen, absence of direct token-efficient baseline comparisons, and limited evidence about routing. The expanded comparisons, per-dataset results, and reproducibility information substantially improve assessment of the central contribution. Benefits are qualified by overbroad performance interpretations and router-reporting inconsistencies: recall labels conflict with Figure 3, and its prediction totals differ from Table 7. These flaws weaken parts of the analysis but do not outweigh the substantial empirical and documentation gains.
